label: TRENDnet TPE-TG160g
description: TRENDnet TPE-TG160g (v4) - sixteen-port unmanaged gigabit PoE+ rack switch: 16x 10/100/1000 PoE+ RJ45 at up to 30 W each against a 246 W budget, 32 Gbps switching capacity, DIP switch for VLAN port isolation, storm control and 250 m extend mode on ports 1-8, smart fans, internal PSU, 1U 19-inch housing.

poe.note: PoE standard 802.3af/at on all 16 ports, up to 30 W per port, 246 W total budget - the vendor states it as supplying up to 16 Power over Ethernet devices with up to 30 W per port, which is 480 W of port capability against a 246 W budget. 246 W is 16 x 15.4 W, so 802.3af on every port fits and only about eight ports can run at 802.3at at once. The budget, not the port count, is the limit.

fabric.note: Vendor switching capacity of 32 Gbps, the full-duplex aggregate of sixteen gigabit ports.

notes: TRENDnet TPE-TG160g v4 figures from the product page (https://www.trendnet.com/products/unmanaged-poe-switch/16-port-gigabit-poeplus-switch-TPE-TG160g-v4). Hardware: 16x gigabit PoE+ ports, 32 Gbps switching capacity, internal power supply, 1U 19-inch rack-mountable metal housing with brackets in the box, smart fans, 0-40 C operating range, 3 kg. The DIP switch offers VLAN port isolation (traffic separated between ports) and storm control, and turns ports 1-8 into 250 m / 820 ft PoE+ runs at 10 Mbps - that is a physical toggle, not 802.1Q: the box has no management interface, no CLI, no per-VLAN configuration and no SFP cages, so this spec declares l2-forward and nothing beyond it. The extend-mode rate drop is a port setting, not a separate interface.
